Hi Ava,

We're evaluating Redwood for a patient-facing summarization feature and need to lock down a few privacy/processing items before legal will clear a pilot. Quick questions:

- Can Redwood commit in the DPA that customer-provided prompts and generated responses will not be used to further train or improve models (no-training / model-improvement opt-out)?
- If yes, what form does that commitment take (DPA clause + appendix, or a customer-level toggle in the Console)?
- Who owns the prompts and generated outputs from the integration? Nimbus needs to ensure all outputs are Nimbus IP and that there are no implied rights to reuse them.
- Please attach the latest subprocessor list and clarify whether subprocessor transfers (particularly US->EU) are covered by SCCs or standard contractual mechanisms.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and high-level KMS/crypto statements for encryption-at-rest/in-transit.

We're on a fairly aggressive timeline but want the privacy guarantees in writing before proceeding.

Thanks,

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear summary and context. Short answers up front: we can provide a contractual "no-model-improvement" commitment and we also document customer ownership of prompts and outputs. Details below and next steps at the end.

1) No-training / model-improvement opt-out
- We offer a DPA Appendix (Appendix C) that records a customer-level "no-model-improvement" selection. When selected, Redwood will ensure customer data (prompts/responses/metadata) is excluded from model training or tuning pipelines.
- Implementation: this is enforced by routing and storage controls (dedicated ingestion flags + truncated telemetry) and is auditable via exportable logs.
- Operational note: customers can choose the no-train option for specific environments (e.g., production only). There is no automatic charge for the setting itself, though some use-cases that require isolated pipelines or extra retention controls may incur nominal operational fees; we can scope that in the SOW.

2) Ownership of prompts / outputs
- Contractually: the DPA + Master Services Agreement (MSA) includes a clause stating the customer retains all rights in their input and generated output, and Redwood is granted a limited license only to process requests for the purposes of providing the service. We do not claim ownership of customer outputs.

3) Subprocessors & transfers
- Attached: Subprocessor_List_2026.pdf — this is our current list. For transfers, we rely on SCCs (EU) and an internal transfer governance process. We can add a DPA section that enumerates which subprocessors will handle EU data and provide commitment to route EU-subject-data to EU regions where required.

4) Evidence requested (SOC 2, KMS)
- Attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.docx and a redacted SOC 2 bundle (we typically provide a redacted report; see reference included at the end). We use customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and provide KMS integration details in Appendix D.

Next steps I'd recommend:
- Review the attached DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.docx) and subprocessor list.
- If Nimbus needs a signed no-train appendix, reply with a confirmation and we'll prepare a DocuSign package.
- Please share any redlines from your legal team and we will route to Legal/Privacy for review.

I've CC'd Kimberly (Product Security) to confirm technical routing; she'll reply with specifics if needed.

Best,
Ava Chen

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear redlines and patience while we reviewed this internally. Good news: Redwood can commit to the following, and we've prepared a final package for signature.

- No-model-improvement (no-train): Redwood will not use, access, retain, or otherwise process customer-provided prompts or generated outputs for the purpose of improving, tuning, or training models outside the scope of providing the service, except as required by law. This is captured in Appendix C of the attached signed DPA.
- Ownership: The DPA/MSA reiterates that Nimbus retains all rights in inputs and outputs; Redwood only receives a limited processing license to provide the service.
- Audit: We will provide an annual, redacted audit export showing routing flags, retention events, and tenant-level telemetry. The audit deliverable will be under NDA and will be scoped to remove PII and message bodies; hashes and metadata (timestamps, ingestion flags, storage location) will be included for verification.
- EU routing: When the no-train selection is enabled and the account requests EU-only processing, we will pin processing to our eu-west region and commit to SCCs for transfers where necessary. If Nimbus requires dedicated capacity in-region, we'll include that as an optional addendum (SOW).
- Subprocessors: See Subprocessor_List_2026.pdf; we will also provide a filtered subprocessor table showing which providers may plausibly access plaintext outputs (and the access controls required).

I've attached the signed DPA (Signed_DPA_Nimbus.pdf) and a DocuSign package link to the final Appendix. Please sign and we'll turn on the account-level no-train flag and confirm region pinning.
